He and his wife, Lisa, owned the business before their son Dan bought it in 2014, when the company operated 35 locations across northern Ohio.

long_biography.plain_text:
Edwin “Mick” Coles entered petroleum distribution by exercising an option to buy Wakeman Oil in 1982. He sought bank financing for the acquisition, with his lawyer and accountant participating in discussions. Subsequent loans supported the oil business and other companies owned by Coles and his wife, Lisa.

The couple also became owners of Dancing Pedlar Farm in Virginia. Its Angus breeding programme combined assessment of the animals’ physical qualities with genomic testing, under general manager Kevin Fleenor. The farm offered breeding cattle through online production sales and brought in guest consignors, including the Virginia breeder Daltons on the Sycamore.
